senses.definition: A loud exclamation intended to scare someone. Usually used when one has been hidden from the target, and then appears unexpectedly.
An exclamation used by a member of an audience, as at a stage play or sporting event, to indicate derision or disapproval.

quotes.text: I ask them to record their votes in my favour, and I ask, is there any man who will dare to call me a stranger (hear, hear, and booing)?
quotes.reference: 1852 July 15, “Dundalk Election”, in The Freeman's Journal, volume lxxxv, Dublin, page 3:

senses.definition: A derisive shout of the word 'boo' made to indicate disapproval.

quotes.text: ...Hodgson headed down the tunnel with the boos of fans ringing in his ears after an eighth league defeat of the season...
quotes.reference: 2010 December 29, Sam Sheringham, “Liverpool 0 - 1 Wolverhampton”, in BBC Sport:

quotes.text: Like a moustachioed pantomime villain relishing boos and hisses from the audience, Trump is oblivious to warnings and protestations from the sane world and simply contemptuous of the lickspittle mob desperately hoping to go unnoticed.
quotes.reference: 2026 January 24, Michael Pascoe, “America’s mighty economic power has feet of clay”, in Michael West Media:

examples: When he took the podium, the crowd booed.

quotes.text: Substitute Charlie Austin scored seven minutes into his Southampton debut as a lacklustre Manchester United were booed off at Old Trafford.
quotes.reference: 2016 January 23, Phil Dakwes, “Man Utd 0–1 Southampton”, in BBC Sport:

senses.definition: (transitive) To shout extended boos at, as a form of disapproval or derision.
examples: The protesters loudly booed the visiting senator.

senses.definition: (US, Canada, African-American Vernacular, slang) A close acquaintance or significant other.

quotes.text: A tall, hooded young woman, clutching a newspaper article, delivered a note to the judge. “My name is Sunkist,” she wrote, “Lionel R. Harris is my boyfriend. Lewis shot my Boo and it was not self-defense . . . . Judge and jurors please listen to me I am 17 years of {age} and a good young lady and my Boo got killed for nothing.”

senses.definition: (now rare, Northern England, intransitive) To make a sound characteristic of cattle; to moo.

quotes.text: The cow's tether is put about the neck of the individual who has lost the cow, and he must go about booing like a cow till atonement is made.

senses.definition: A tail feather from an ostrich.

quotes.text: Burglary.—On Monday night or early on Tuesday morning, some thieves effected an entrance into the premises of Mr. W. J. Laybourne, ostrich feather manufacturer, 60, St. John-street, West Smithfield, and carried off 1,000 prime white feathers, 500 long single black, 800 double ditto, 3,000 mixed colours, 500 spadones, 300 white plumes, 300 coloured boos, and 400 long white light feminas, which, with other property, were valued at about £4,000.
quotes.reference: 1877 June 15, The Leeds Mercury, volume 114, number 12,225, Leeds, West Yorkshire, page 2, column 5:

quotes.text: White Boos declined 10s. to 15s. per lb.; Femina Boos 2s. 6d. to 5s. per lb., and drab Boos about 2s. 6d. per lb.
quotes.reference: 1891 February 1, “Report on the December Public Sales of Ostrich and Osprey Feathers, Bird Skins, &c.”, in The Humming Bird: A Monthly Scientific, Artistic, and Industrial Review, volume I., number 2, page 16, column 1:

quotes.text: The usual kinds of ostrich feathers known to the trade come into the Tripoli market. These are whites, blacks, feminas, byocks, spadonas, boos, drabs and floss.
